subject: Question about probabilistic selection task results

messages.author: 74fe1c9da24adb5a
messages.subject: Question about probabilistic selection task results
parts:
Hi,


As someone who has had no prior experience of coding, your package has been very user-friendly and useful. In our study, participants were asked to complete the probabilistic selection task with 180 trials (3 blocks of 60 trials), matched as close to the original task (as used in Frank et al., 2004; 2007) but I had some questions about the results obtained from the gain/loss learning Q model. 


The model showed MCMC convergence with Rhat values= 1.00 for all subjects (trace plots attached), however, all values for the mu_alpha_negative parameters were 0.00- I wasn’t sure if this is due to the chains being stuck to the lower bound or whether this was due to variability in responses/poor model fit or some other reason. 


I have tried modelling the data with only the first block (60 trials) and changing the parameter bounds (e.g. loss= -1; reward= 5 and loss= -5) all without any luck. I’ve attached the trace plots, group-level posterior distributions and pairs plots, along with the sample data (n=50). I would be grateful for your thoughts and any recommendations.


Thank you for your help, once again your package has been incredibly helpful!


Best,


Rowan

output1$fit@stanmodel
S4 class stanmodel 'pst_gainloss_Q' coded as follows:
#include /pre/license.stan

data {
  int<lower=1> N;             // Number of subjects
  int<lower=1> T;             // Maximum # of trials
  int<lower=1> Tsubj[N];      // # of trials for acquisition phase

  int<lower=-1,upper=6> option1[N, T];
  int<lower=-1,upper=6> option2[N, T];
  int<lower=-1,upper=1> choice[N, T];
  real reward[N, T];
}

transformed data {
  // Default values to initialize the vector of expected values
  vector[6] initial_values;
  initial_values = rep_vector(0, 6);
}

parameters {
  // Group-level parameters
  vector[3] mu_pr;
  vector<lower=0>[3] sigma;

  // Subject-level parameters for Matt trick
  vector[N] alpha_pos_pr;
  vector[N] alpha_neg_pr;
  vector[N] beta_pr;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector<lower=0,upper=1>[N] alpha_pos;
  vector<lower=0,upper=1>[N] alpha_neg;
  vector<lower=0,upper=10>[N] beta;

  alpha_pos = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1] + sigma[1] * alpha_pos_pr);
  alpha_neg = Phi_approx(mu_pr[2] + sigma[2] * alpha_neg_pr);
  beta      = Phi_approx(mu_pr[3] + sigma[3] * beta_pr) * 10;
}

model {
  // Priors for group-level parameters
  mu_pr    ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma ~ normal(0, 0.2);

  // Priors for subject-level parameters
  alpha_pos_pr ~ normal(0, 1);
  alpha_neg_pr ~ normal(0, 1);
  beta_pr      ~ normal(0, 1);

  for (i in 1:N) {
    int co;         // Chosen option
    real delta;     // Difference between two options
    real pe;        // Prediction error
    real alpha;
    vector[6] ev;   // Expected values

    ev = initial_values;

    // Acquisition Phase
    for (t in 1:Tsubj[i]) {
      co = (choice[i, t] > 0) ? option1[i, t] : option2[i, t];

      // Luce choice rule
      delta = ev[option1[i, t]] - ev[option2[i, t]];
      target += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(choice[i, t] | beta[i] * delta);

      pe = reward[i, t] - ev[co];
alpha = ( reward[i, t] > 0) ? alpha_pos[i] : alpha_neg[i];

ev[co] += alpha * pe;
    }
  }
}

generated quantities {
  // For group-level parameters
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  mu_alpha_pos;
  real<lower=0,upper=1>  mu_alpha_neg;
  real<lower=0,upper=10> mu_beta;

  // For log-likelihood calculation
  real log_lik[N];

  mu_alpha_pos = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1]);
  mu_alpha_neg = Phi_approx(mu_pr[2]);
  mu_beta      = Phi_approx(mu_pr[3]) * 10;

  {
    for (i in 1:N) {
      int co;         // Chosen option
      real delta;     // Difference between two options
      real pe;        // Prediction error
      real alpha;
      vector[6] ev;   // Expected values

      ev = initial_values;
      log_lik[i] = 0;

      // Acquisition Phase
      for (t in 1:Tsubj[i]) {
        co = (choice[i, t] > 0) ? option1[i, t] : option2[i, t];

        // Luce choice rule
        delta = ev[option1[i, t]] - ev[option2[i, t]];
        log_lik[i] += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(choice[i, t] | beta[i] * delta);

        pe = reward[i, t] - ev[co];
alpha = ( reward[i, t] > 0) ? alpha_pos[i] : alpha_neg[i];
ev[co] += alpha * pe;

}
    }
  }
}

        delta = ev[option1[i, t]] - ev[option2[i, t]];
        log_lik[i] += bernoulli_logit_lpmf(choice[i, t] | beta[i] * delta);

        pe = reward[i, t] - ev[co];
        alpha = ( reward[i, t] > 0) ? alpha_pos[i] : alpha_neg[i];
        ev[co] += alpha * pe;
      }
    }
  }
}
